title: mcpx(source): a symlink loop entry aborts the whole @dir: resolve — ELOOP is neither skipped like a dangling link nor pinned like a permission error

body:
## Problem

In mcpx's directory source walk, one symlink loop entry makes the whole `@dir:` resolve fail — while the two neighboring bad-link cases are tolerated:

- a **dangling** symlink is skipped (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/source.go:174-180`: `os.Stat` failure is continued past only when `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)`, comment "A dangling link has no regular target to read");
- a **directory** cycle (a dir symlink pointing back to an ancestor) is skipped by the `os.SameFile` ancestor guard in the same walk (`source.go:152-157`);
- a symlink **loop** (a link to itself, or two links pointing at each other) makes `os.Stat` fail with ELOOP ("too many levels of symbolic links"), which is neither of the above: `source.go:181` returns the error and the entire directory resolution aborts with zero files read — including every healthy regular file sitting next to the loop.

A loop link, like a dangling link, has no regular target to read. The current split — tolerate a missing target and a directory cycle, but let a loop target deny the whole source — is an untested gap, not a pinned decision: the pinned cases in the shipped tests are dangling-skip (`source_test.go:245` `TestDirectorySkipsDanglingLinkAndFollowsLinkOutsideRoot`), directory-cycle-safety (`source_test.go:191`), and permission-error propagation (`source_unix_test.go:73` `TestDirectoryReportsInaccessibleSymlinkTarget`, which pins EACCES as a returned error and must keep behaving that way). No test covers the ELOOP case.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, main 8a0a1c0ceac8)

Probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-mcpx-eloop` on the laptop: the real `pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/source.go` copied verbatim (md5 `768194633188160a349eafd555defe53`, identical to the file on main) into a standalone module, driven through the exported `source.Resolve("@dir:"+root, …)`:

- control (regular.ts + dangling.ts → missing): resolves OK, files = [regular.ts] — matches the shipped pin;
- self-loop (regular.ts + loop.ts → loop.ts): **fails** — `reading …/loop.ts: stat …/loop.ts: too many levels of symbolic links`, zero files returned;
- pair loop (regular.ts + a.ts → b.ts, b.ts → a.ts): **fails** the same way at a.ts, zero files returned;
- control (directory back-link to the root itself): resolves OK, files = [regular.ts] — the ancestor guard tolerates the directory cycle.

So one stray looped link (easily produced by a bad `ln -s` pair or a tool that links a directory's contents into itself at file level) takes down every launcher/prefix/hook that reads its source from that directory, with an error that names the link but gives no way to keep the healthy remainder.

Related: closed #1727 covered non-regular files in directory sources (FIFO/socket/symlink-to-directory); this is the distinct remaining Stat-error class for file entries. The Go source lives only in this repo (`pkgs/mcpx`); dezren39/darwin-nix only wraps/launches the built mcpx, so no cross-repo set applies. Found via a pr-diff-review REVIEW-FINDING on PR #3744 that was left as decide-and-test material; verified independently this run before filing.

## Why it matters

`@dir:` sources feed mcpx launchers, prefixes, and error hooks. A single looped symlink — which the directory-cycle guard already proves the walk intends to survive at directory level — currently denies the whole source instead of just the unreadable entry. Robustness here should be uniform: an entry with no readable regular target is skipped (dangling, loop), while genuinely informative errors (permission) still surface, per the existing pin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A directory containing a self-loop symlink or a mutually-looping symlink pair, plus at least one regular file, resolves successfully and returns exactly the regular files (the loop entries skipped), for both the self-loop and pair-loop shapes.
- [ ] Regression tests for both loop shapes land in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/source` (mirroring the style of `TestDirectorySkipsDanglingLinkAndFollowsLinkOutsideRoot`), and fail on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] The pinned permission behavior is unchanged: `TestDirectoryReportsInaccessibleSymlinkTarget` still passes — only the ELOOP class changes disposition, not EACCES or other Stat errors (or, if the fix deliberately widens/narrows which Stat errors skip, the disposition of each class is named in the PR and the affected pins updated with rationale).
- [ ] The existing source suite (`go test ./pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/...`, or the package's normal CI route) is green with the new tests.
